body.p: This response is being filed in reply to the non-final Office Action dated October 21, 2024. In that Office Action, claims 1-8 and 13-19 were rejected, and claims 9-12 and 20 were objected to for being dependent on a base claim but otherwise allowable if rewritten into independent form. Claims 1, 8, 10, 18, and 20 are being amended. Therefore, claims 1-20 remain pending in the application.

Claims 1-2, 7, 14, 16-19 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as being anticipated by Velazquez Alcantar et al. (U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 20210078581). This rejection is respectfully traversed for the reasons discussed below.
Each of independent claims 1 and 18 is being amended to recite, inter alia:

determining whether the first torque request is not satisfiable by comparing the first torque request with a first shaped torque request to determine a first error therebetween, the first torque request being determined to be not satisfiable if the first error is

greater than a first error threshold for the first torque source; [and] determining whether the second torque request is not satisfiable by comparing the second torque request with a second shaped torque request to determine a second error therebetween, the second torque request being determined to be not satisfiable if the second error is greater than a second error threshold for the second
torque source.
This subject matter is not taught or rendered obvious by Velazquez Alcantar, at least for the reasons below.

Velazquez Alcantar does not explicitly teach or suggest determining whether the first or second torque requests are not satisfiable by comparing them with shaped torque requests to determine errors and then evaluating these errors against thresholds. Velazquez Alcantar is primarily directed to controlling wheel slip in electric or hybrid vehicles by switching between torque control mode and speed control mode in response to wheel slip. Velazquez Alcantar focuses on the operation of electric machines on the vehicle's axles and how they respond to conditions like wheel slip,
vehicle yaw rate, and split-Mu conditions. There appears to be no mention of comparing torque requests with shaped torque requests or evaluating errors against thresholds in this context.

Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that Velazquez Alcantar fails to teach or render obvious claims 1 or 18 as amended. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the present rejection be withdrawn, and that claims 1 and 3-16 be allowed.

Claims 3-6 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Velazquez Alcantar et al. in view of Aswani et al. (U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 20090234551). This rejection is respectfully traversed for the reasons discussed below.

Claims 8, 13 and 15 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Velazquez Alcantar et al. in view of Heap et al. (U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 20090112385). This rejection is respectfully traversed for the reasons discussed below.

Aswani and Heap were cited solely in connection with subject matter of dependent claims 3-6, 8, 13, and 15. Aswani and Heap do not make up for the deficiencies of Velazquez Alcantar with respect to independent claims 1 and 18. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 3-6, 8, 13, and 15 are allowed at least because of their dependency on claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be withdrawn and that claims 3-6, 8, 13, and 15 be allowed along with the other pending claims.

Claims 9-12 and 20 are objected to for being dependent on a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten into independent form, including any intervening claims. Claim 20 is being rewritten into independent form, including the subject matter of intervening claims 7 and 8. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 20 is allowable and respectfully ask that it be allowed.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims are allowable over the prior art. Reconsideration is therefore requested. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned if doing so would advance prosecution of this case.
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge Deposit Account No. 50-0852 for any required fees or to credit that same deposit account with any overpayment associated with this communication.
Respectfully submitted,
REISING ETHINGTON P.C.
/James D. Stevens Jr.!
